phase: E1 - is the Stage-2 fragmentation the deferred hatch-style defect?
method: HatchUNet predicted-hatch fraction of ink, on the 12 Stage-2 gated figures and 20 that pass
verdict: PARTIAL, not general. Four of seven fragmented figures carry substantial predicted hatch (15.8% to 51.2% against a 6.3% baseline), but the two MOST fragmented -- micro ratios of 0.82 and 0.95 -- carry essentially none, so their fragmentation has a different cause. A median-only reading would have called this hatch-driven and overstated it.
note: On the figures where hatch IS predicted at 47-51%, the detector is firing and the figure still gates, so removal is not preventing fragmentation. That is a different defect from the missed bold/solid styles the owner flagged.
recommendation: E2 (extend HatchUNet training styles, 3-5 days including labelling) would address at most 4 of 12 gated figures, about 4% of the cohort, and only if the cause there is detection rather than removal. Deprioritised on that return. E1 cost half a day and was worth it precisely for producing this answer.
